title: POPANE-R1 Independent Prospective Valence Increment Replication
purpose: Independently test whether peripheral physiology improves future continuous valence forecasting beyond an extremely strong simple persistence benchmark, using public POPANE Study 6 after the CASE O002 result.
scientific_scope: External valence-only replication. It does not test arousal and does not test causal or phenomenal claims.

file_inclusion.include: Segment CSVs whose filename is <participant>_<segment>.csv, excluding _All and _Baseline.
file_inclusion.segment_rule: Before reading values, include only segment labels appearing in >=20 distinct participants according to filenames.
file_inclusion.participant_rule: Use all participants with >=1 technically usable included segment.
technical_segment_qc: timestamp strictly nondecreasing after numeric coercion
duration >=55 seconds so all horizons can contribute at least one anchor
ECG finite fraction >=0.80 OR EDA finite fraction >=0.80
no exclusion based on affect magnitude, physiology magnitude, prediction error, or condition outcome

sampling.source_rate: Metadata reports timestamp/affect/ECG/ICG/EDA/marker at 1000 Hz; hemodynamics beat-to-beat.
sampling.anchors: Within each usable segment, anchors every 10 seconds starting 10 s after segment start, while the requested target window remains inside segment.
sampling.target: Mean affect over target window. POPANE Study 6 'affect' is continuous valence per the data descriptor.

baseline.primary_naive: y_hat = mean affect in [-5,-1] s. No training.
baseline.fitted_context: Ridge prediction from prior affect + normalized time within segment; segment identity omitted in joint unseen-segment tests.

ECG: R-peak count using a fixed preprocessing/peak rule implemented before results
mean heart rate from detected R-R intervals
physiology_features.missingness: Per-feature training-fold median imputation only. Feature values are never imputed using test-fold statistics.
physiology_features.scaling: Training-fold standardization for Ridge; no scaling required for tree learner.

ridge.tuning: training-only GroupKFold by participant, max 4 folds

generalization.subject_folds: 10 deterministic folds made by sorting numeric participant IDs and assigning round-robin fold index; all windows from a participant stay together.
generalization.primary_joint: For each subject fold × eligible segment label, train excludes every participant in the held subject fold AND every row of the held segment label; test only held-fold rows of that segment. Segment identity is omitted from features.
generalization.secondary_subject_only: 10-fold held-person evaluation using all other participants. Segment label may be one-hot encoded only in this secondary analysis because segment labels are seen in training.
generalization.rationale: Primary mirrors the CASE G1 simultaneous unseen-person × unseen-stimulus logic while remaining computationally tractable.

for_each_horizon_and_learner: delta_naive_phys = MAE(naive)-MAE(physiology), positive favors physiology over simple persistence
delta_fitted_phys = MAE(fitted prior/context)-MAE(physiology), positive favors incremental physiology beyond learned baseline
endpoints.uncertainty: Participant-cluster bootstrap with 5000 resamples of participant-level mean paired MAE differences; primary unit is participant, preserving within-person segment/window dependence.
endpoints.descriptive: Also report segment-level and overall row-weighted MAE, but do not use them to override primary participant-cluster inference.

decisions.CLEAR_EXTERNAL_PHYSIOLOGY_INCREMENT: For at least one horizon, BOTH Ridge and HGB have delta_naive_phys 95% CI strictly above zero in primary joint generalization. This contradicts a horizon-invariant no-increment claim and requires the CASE paper claim to be narrowed.
decisions.REPLICATED_NONPOSITIVE_INCREMENT_PATTERN: No horizon has delta_naive_phys 95% CI strictly above zero for either learner, and mean delta_naive_phys <=0 at >=3 of 4 horizons for both learners.
decisions.STRONG_REPLICATION_OF_BASELINE_DOMINANCE: REPLICATED_NONPOSITIVE_INCREMENT_PATTERN plus naive persistence has lower overall MAE than physiology for both learners at all four horizons.

secondary_checks: feature-family ablation ECG-only, EDA-only, ICG/hemodynamic-only only after the primary result and labeled secondary
anti_leakage: No predictor sample at or after target start.
All preprocessing/imputation/scaling/tuning fit only on training data.
No participant leakage across subject folds.
Primary joint test excludes the held segment label entirely from training.
No data-derived choice of horizon, segment, feature family, learner or exclusion rule after outcome inspection.
privacy_reproducibility: Do not commit raw POPANE files or participant-level raw signals to GitHub.
Commit code/protocol and aggregate result summaries only.
Transient derived feature tables may remain workflow artifacts for limited retention in the private repository.
Cite POPANE and respect CC BY-NC 4.0.
firewalls: A nonpositive predictive increment does not imply physiology is causally irrelevant to feeling.
It does not imply body-independence of emotion.
It does not prove that affect is generated by self-report persistence.
It does not support phenomenal or consciousness claims.
External valence replication cannot by itself establish the same result for arousal.
paper_gate: If the nonpositive pattern replicates in POPANE under the primary joint test and survives both learners, upgrade the benchmark/identifiability result to a serious paper candidate; still perform final systematic novelty and reporting/leakage audit before manuscript-ready classification.
